question: A 55-year-old man comes to the physician because of fatigue and worsening abdominal pain for 4 weeks. He also reports excessive night sweats and a 5.4-kg (12-lb) weight loss during this time. He has a neck swelling for 4 days. Physical examination shows a nontender, enlarged, and fixed supraclavicular lymph node. There is splenomegaly. A CT scan of the thorax and abdomen shows massively enlarged axillary, mediastinal, and cervical lymph nodes. Analysis of an excised cervical lymph node shows lymphocytes with a high proliferative index that stain positive for CD20. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?
reasoning_chain: CHAIN: "55-year-old man with fatigue and abdominal pain" -> "weight loss and night sweats" -> "enlarged supraclavicular lymph node" -> "splenomegaly present" -> "CT scan shows enlarged lymph nodes" -> "lymph node analysis shows high proliferative index lymphocytes" -> "CD20 positive staining indicates B-cell origin" -> "most likely diagnosis is Diffuse large B-cell lymphoma" -> 85%

CHAIN: "55-year-old man with systemic symptoms" -> "presence of nontender, fixed supraclavicular lymph node" -> "CT scan reveals extensive lymphadenopathy" -> "lymph node biopsy shows high proliferative index" -> "CD20 positivity suggests B-cell malignancy" -> "considering age and symptoms, Diffuse large B-cell lymphoma is likely" -> 80%

CHAIN: "Patient presents with significant weight loss and night sweats" -> "physical exam reveals enlarged lymph nodes and splenomegaly" -> "CT scan confirms extensive lymphadenopathy" -> "biopsy shows lymphocytes with high proliferative index" -> "CD20 positive indicates a B-cell lymphoma" -> "most consistent with Diffuse large B-cell lymphoma" -> 90%

CHAIN: "Symptoms of fatigue, weight loss, and night sweats" -> "enlarged supraclavicular lymph node found" -> "CT scan shows multiple enlarged lymph nodes" -> "biopsy reveals high proliferative index lymphocytes" -> "CD20 positive suggests B-cell lineage" -> "less likely to be Hodgkin lymphoma due to age and findings" -> "most likely diagnosis is Diffuse large B-cell lymphoma" -> 75%
analysis: The patient's symptoms of fatigue, night sweats, weight loss, and the presence of a fixed supraclavicular lymph node, along with splenomegaly and massively enlarged lymph nodes, suggest a lymphoproliferative disorder. The excised lymph node analysis shows lymphocytes with a high proliferative index that stain positive for CD20, indicating a B-cell lineage. Among the options, Diffuse large B-cell lymphoma (DLBCL) is characterized by a high proliferation rate and CD20 positivity, making it the most likely diagnosis in this case.
